sections.title: Mission · Create and Manage Identities
paragraphs: Linux administrators create and manage users, groups, numeric identities, passwords, and default user files.
sections.callout: CREATE THE IDENTITY · ASSIGN THE GROUP · SECURE THE PASSWORD

sections.title: Users Have Numeric Identities
paragraphs: Linux identifies users internally with a numeric UID. The username is human-readable; the UID is the system's numeric identity.
sections.callout: USERNAME = HUMAN NAME · UID = LINUX IDENTITY NUMBER

sections.title: Why UIDs Matter
paragraphs: File ownership and access decisions ultimately refer to numeric IDs. Names make administration readable, while UIDs bind permissions to identities.

sections.title: Groups
paragraphs: Groups collect users so access can be assigned to multiple accounts efficiently.

sections.title: useradd
paragraphs: useradd creates a new user account and can set account properties depending on its options and system defaults.

sections.title: passwd
paragraphs: The passwd command sets or changes account passwords and supports password-management tasks.

sections.title: Exam Trap · passwd vs. /etc/passwd
paragraphs: passwd is a command for password management. /etc/passwd is the user account information file.

sections.title: /etc/passwd
paragraphs: /etc/passwd stores general account information including username and UID.

sections.title: /etc/shadow
paragraphs: /etc/shadow protects password hashes and password-aging data.

sections.title: /etc/group
paragraphs: /etc/group stores group definitions and membership information.

sections.title: /etc/skel/
paragraphs: /etc/skel/ contains skeleton files copied into a newly created user's home directory.
sections.callout: SKEL = STARTER FILES FOR NEW USERS

sections.title: Why /etc/skel/ Matters
paragraphs: Administrators can place default profiles, configuration, and starter files in /etc/skel/ so new users receive a consistent environment.

sections.title: User Creation Is More Than a Username
paragraphs: A complete user identity can involve a UID, primary and supplementary groups, home directory, shell, password, and copied skeleton files.

sections.title: GSA Scenario Recognition
bullets: Set or change a password → passwd
Default files for new home directories → /etc/skel/

entries.title: passwd vs. /etc/passwd
paragraphs: passwd is the password command; /etc/passwd is the user account file.

entries.title: useradd vs. groupadd
paragraphs: useradd creates a user; groupadd creates a group.

entries.title: Username vs. UID
paragraphs: Username is human-readable; UID is the numeric Linux identity.

entries.title: /etc/skel/
paragraphs: It stores new-user skeleton files, not passwords, logs, or device information.

sections.title: Maestro Recognition Sheet
sections.callout: USERADD USER · GROUPADD GROUP · PASSWD PASSWORD · UID NUMBER · SKEL STARTER KIT
